analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved quarantine and surveillance practices for non-human primates (NHPs) due to their role in preclinical research and the zoonotic risks they pose. The background highlights the increasing use of NHPs in research and the associated risks of viral pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review comparing national quarantine frameworks for NHPs, examining pathogen-specific features, and discussing their implications for quarantine and surveillance. It focuses on the biological and epidemiological characteristics of major viral pathogens relevant to disease surveillance and control in NHPs.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a comparative analysis of national quarantine policies, pathogen-specific features, and their implications for surveillance and control strategies. The study also considers facility-level responses, occupational health preparedness, and internationally harmonized quarantine standards.
analysis.main_results: The results include the identification of several viral pathogens harbored by NHPs, such as monkeypox virus (MPXV), rabies virus, Marburg virus, Ebola virus, and others. These pathogens are associated with zoonotic risks and can cause clinical manifestations in NHPs similar to those in humans.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that effective quarantine and surveillance are critical for mitigating zoonotic risks and ensuring experimental reproducibility. The novelty lies in the integration of pathogen biology, epidemiology, and international standards to guide risk-based quarantine and infection-control strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of integrated, risk-based quarantine and surveillance strategies for NHPs, which are essential for reducing zoonotic transmission risks and ensuring the reliability of preclinical research. They also highlight the importance of coordinated international efforts in managing these pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base is limited by uneven species coverage, heterogeneity among institutions and surveillance practices, and insufficient data for certain viral pathogens. These limitations suggest a moderate confidence in the conclusions drawn.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the role of non-human primates (NHPs) in preclinical research and the associated zoonotic risks posed by viral pathogens such as monkeypox virus (MPXV). It highlights the need for improved quarantine and surveillance practices, emphasizing the importance of an integrated, risk-based approach. The review compares national quarantine frameworks, discusses pathogen-specific features, and outlines implications for public health and research. Despite the increasing use of NHPs in research, the evidence base remains limited due to variability in surveillance practices and data availability. The findings suggest that coordinated international efforts and facility-level responses are essential for effective disease control and prevention of zoonotic transmission.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在改善非人灵长类动物(NHPs)的检疫和监测实践,因为它们在临床前研究中的作用以及所带来的人兽共患病风险。背景强调了非人灵长类动物在研究中使用量的增加及其相关的病毒病原体风险。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项综述,比较了非人灵长类动物的国家检疫框架,分析了病原体特异性特征,并讨论了其对检疫和监测的影响。它聚焦于与非人灵长类动物疾病监测和控制相关的重大病毒病原体的生物学和流行病学特征。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究的方法包括对国家检疫政策、病原体特异性特征及其对监测和控制策略的影响进行比较分析。此外,还考虑了机构层面的应对措施、职业健康准备以及国际统一的检疫标准。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究结果包括识别了非人灵长类动物携带的多种病毒病原体,例如猴痘病毒(MPXV)、狂犬病毒、马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒等。这些病原体与人兽共患病风险相关,并且在非人灵长类动物中可引起与人类相似的临床表现。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,有效的检疫和监测对于减轻人兽共患病风险和确保实验可重复性至关重要。其创新之处在于将病原体生物学、流行病学以及国际标准整合起来,以指导基于风险的检疫和感染控制策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为非人灵长类动物的整合、基于风险的检疫和监测策略的制定提供了依据,这对于降低人兽共患病风险并确保临床前研究的可靠性至关重要。它们还突显了协调国际努力管理这些病原体的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基础受到物种覆盖不均、机构间和监测实践的异质性以及某些病毒病原体数据不足的限制。这些局限性表明结论的置信度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在改善非人灵长类动物(NHPs)的检疫和监测实践,因为它们在临床前研究中的作用以及所带来的人兽共患病风险。背景强调了非人灵长类动物在研究中使用量的增加及其相关的病毒病原体风险。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项综述,比较了非人灵长类动物的国家检疫框架,分析了病原体特异性特征,并讨论了其对检疫和监测的影响。它聚焦于与非人灵长类动物疾病监测和控制相关的重大病毒病原体的生物学和流行病学特征。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究的方法包括对国家检疫政策、病原体特异性特征及其对监测和控制策略的影响进行比较分析。此外,还考虑了机构层面的应对措施、职业健康准备以及国际统一的检疫标准。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究结果包括识别了非人灵长类动物携带的多种病毒病原体,例如猴痘病毒(MPXV)、狂犬病毒、马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒等。这些病原体与人兽共患病风险相关,并且在非人灵长类动物中可引起与人类相似的临床表现。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,有效的检疫和监测对于减轻人兽共患病风险和确保实验可重复性至关重要。其创新之处在于将病原体生物学、流行病学以及国际标准整合起来,以指导基于风险的检疫和感染控制策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为非人灵长类动物的整合、基于风险的检疫和监测策略的制定提供了依据,这对于降低人兽共患病风险并确保临床前研究的可靠性至关重要。它们还突显了协调国际努力管理这些病原体的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基础受到物种覆盖不均、机构间和监测实践的异质性以及某些病毒病原体数据不足的限制。这些局限性表明结论的置信度中等。

papers.full_text: Considerable knowledge has been generated on the symptoms, course, therapy, and care of survivors of traumatic experiences since posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) was added to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, third edition (DSM-III) in 1980. Notwithstanding this improved understanding, there is still disagreement over the definition, characteristics, and expression of PTSD in various settings. The aim of this paper was to offer a perspective on the limitations of the current conceptualization of mental health problems associated with continuous traumatic stress (CTS), considerations of contextual and cultural differences, and their implications for interventions. Particularly, this perspective aimed to address the generalization of Western therapies in non-Western societies, as well as the limitations of traditional rituals and ceremonies, and their limitations in the treatment of mental illness in the context of unending violent conflicts in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). In many traditional societies in SSA, trauma is experienced and symptoms are appraised based on the culture of survivors, demonstrating the importance of context in the conceptualization of CTS and the design of interventions. Psychological therapies in the majority of Western societies are based on symptom reduction, which are limited in the context of CTS and traditional cultures. The perspective also discusses different ecosystems in the treatment of trauma using Western and traditional society approaches, as well as the unique nature of the violent conflicts in SSA, and suggests a way forward. Finally, we discuss whether Western evidence-based therapies that are locally and culturally grounded and traditional rituals and ceremonies are mutually exclusive, particularly in the context of CTS and mass trauma that uniquely affect individuals, families, communities, and different subpopulations. ConclusionWhile PTSD and CPTSD are invaluable concepts in understanding the experiences of individuals who endured traumatic events, they may be limited for societies experiencing unending protracted violent conflicts. Comprehending the functional deficits associated with experiencing traumatic events and understanding the daily challenges that affect survivors, both at the community and individual levels, numerous stakeholders (e.g., individuals, families, the community, and cultural leaders) may be required in the design of interventions. Of critical importance is the reconstruction of the social fabric and pillars that once held societies together and are responsible for the diagnosis, prognosis, and care of survivors. In light of the complexity in the conceptualization of CTS in many theaters of conflicts in SSA where protracted traumatic events are dominant, a more contextualized and nuanced understanding of traumatic reactions may provide better treatment outcomes.Interventions to aid war-affected communities in regaining security, normalcy, and control while promoting community involvement and mobilizing internal resources to fulfill their needs are essential (48). Where the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of mental health problems include the entire community; thus, interventions must be guided by conceptual clarity, contextual considerations, and community involvement. In many ethnic groups in SSA, healing is a systemic process that occurs at the individual, family, and community levels. Enhancing resilience, empowering individuals, and developing family and community capacities to help survivors deal with ongoing stressors are key pillars to sustaining the wellbeing of war-affected populations. IntroductionPosttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is the most prevalent mental disorder in the aftermath of violent conflicts. Since the inclusion of PTSD in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, third edition (DSM-III) in 1980, considerable knowledge has been generated about its symptoms, trajectory, treatment, and care (1). This increased knowledge notwithstanding, the definition, characteristics, and manifestations of PTSD in different contexts continue to be contentious (2). The differences in the PTSD definitions between the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition Text Revision (DSM-5-TR) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) demonstrate this contention (3, 4).The DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 conceptualize PTSD somewhat differently. The DSM-5-TR organizes PTSD symptoms into four clusters: intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and alterations in arousal and reactivity (3). ICD-11 uses a narrower formulation centered on re-experiencing the traumatic event in the present, deliberate avoidance, and a persistent sense of current threat (4). Nevertheless, the ICD-11 construct was developed to specifically capture the sequelae of new concepts of sustained, repeated, and inescapable trauma such as complex posttraumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) (1). The CPTSD diagnosis that includes the additional three symptom groups (e.g., affective, relationship, and self-concept changes) is an improvement of the narrowly defined PTSD diagnosis. According to the WHO development goals for ICD-11, a CPTSD diagnosis is clinically practical and has demonstrated acceptable psychodiagnostic properties in several research studies, including good differentiation from other disorders such as personality disorder with borderline type (5).Despite these developments, CPTSD and ICD-11 remain disorders arising after exposure to extremely threatening or horrific past events. Moreover, their application becomes more complex when the source of the threatening or horrific events remains active because responses such as heightened vigilance or even relationship changes may represent both traumatic distress and a realistic adaptation to the continuing threat.While PTSD has been studied internationally, its dominant conceptual and diagnostic frameworks were initially developed largely within North American and European psychiatric traditions (6). Global diagnostic categories facilitate communication, research comparisons, and access to treatment, but they do not eliminate the need to consider cultural and contextual differences in the experience and expression of distress. Culture may influence how symptoms are interpreted and appraised and the language used to describe suffering, the people approached for assistance, and the interventions considered legitimate. Evidence-based psychological interventions have demonstrated benefits among conflict-affected populations in SSA (7, 8). However, treatments focused on symptom reduction alone may be insufficient where traumatic stress continues to be generated by insecurity, displacement, poverty, disrupted livelihoods, and damaged social relationships such as in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo), South Sudan, and northern Nigeria. The central issue, however, is not about the origin of interventions (e.g., the West or SSA), but whether the interventions adequately respond to the cultural, social, and material contexts and the conditions in which the distress occurs.Estimates of the frequency of PTSD vary widely from 0% to 74%, especially in SSA (9). This variation is mainly driven by measurement heterogeneity, population selection, and timing (e.g., studies conducted during conflicts). The pooled prevalence of likely PTSD is estimated to be 22%, 30% in people who have experienced conflict, and 8% in those who have not experienced conflict, according to a prior systematic review and meta-analyses (9). Current theories of PTSD are predicated on the notion that the traumatic events happened in the past (10). However, in conflicts such as those in DR Congo or South Sudan, people experience severe psychological effects of constantly being in danger, as opposed to responding to a prior occurrence, as in PTSD. Systemic violence, ongoing domestic abuse, and active violent conflicts are common drivers of continuous traumatic stress (CTS) (11). In addition, contrary to typical PTSD, CTS is persistent, putting victims in a continuous state of vigilance and survival.Particularly in the Great Lakes region (Burundi, the DR Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, etc.), millions of people live in a time of continuous peril and uncertainty due to violent conflicts, forced relocation, and epidemics such as Ebola virus disease, Marburg virus disease, and monkeypox (mpox) (12). Consequently, these traumatic stressors present distinct difficulties for diagnosis and interventions. While PTSD has been well described and characterized, CTS is still underdeveloped in psychological frameworks, literature, and intervention designs despite its importance in a variety of global situations, including communities dealing with systematic violence and in war-torn areas such as the DR Congo, Somalia, South Sudan, and the Sudan, among others.The aim of this paper was to discuss and shape the current debate on the limitations of the current conceptualization of mental illness, considerations of contextual and cultural differences, and their implications for interventions. Particularly, we aimed to address the generalization of Western therapies in non-Western societies and in traditional rituals and ceremonies and their limitations in the treatment of mental illness in the context of CTS. Western-based mental health interventions focus on symptom reduction, whose effectiveness in the context of CTS may fall short of reducing distress. Contextual differences in CTS and possible differences in traditional and cultural expressions, as well as their implications for interventions (6), are described. In addition, although Western therapeutic interventions have shown symptom reduction (e.g., 7, 8), hardly any follow-up studies have demonstrated long-term sustainability in the reduction of symptoms. Lastly, our paper also aimed to shed light on and recognize that traditional rituals and ceremonies in trauma treatment complement culturally adapted and contextually appropriate Western therapies. It is crucial to understand and frame key mental health concepts within specific cultural contexts and design interventions that may help people deal with CTS. Such knowledge and framework should not only reduce symptoms but also systemically empower individuals and families and enhance community resilience in the face of CTS.The War-Affected Youth Survey (WAYS) study and similar studies conducted in northern Uganda and elsewhere in SSA provided the background to this perspective (13). The WAYS study is a longitudinal cohort study of the risks, protective factors, and trajectory of mental health problems in war-affected youths in northern Uganda since 2010, which has several publications. Characteristics and distinctive features of traumatic events in the West and SSASeveral distinct features characterize traumatic events that predispose to traumatic reactions in the Western world and SSA. First, the majority of traumatic events in Europe and North America have a relatively distinct beginning and end; therefore, the concept of ‘post’-traumatic stress disorder may be used with more certainty. On the contrary, in low- and middle-income countries, especially in SSA, protracted wars such as those in South Sudan, the Sudan, the DR Congo, and the Sahel region, lack definite ends (14). Consequently, the diagnosis of PTSD is a challenge because traumatic events are continuous and the affected populations endure extremely stressful situations that continually endanger their lives. For instance, in northern Uganda, post-war environments are rife with a high density of stressors such as gang violence, youth unemployment, stigma against formerly abducted children, land conflicts, domestic violence, and general insecurity even after the guns have fallen silent (15, 16).Second, violent conflicts in SSA have a crippling effect on society, affecting millions of individuals, if not entire communities. Often, the available infrastructure is overwhelmed, humanitarian assistance is overstretched, and the social and traditional resources and the safety net required for coping are severely weakened (17, 18). Importantly, the violent conflicts in SSA target and destroy ways of life, including crucial social, cultural, and material resources that are essential for people to bounce back. Moreover, in spite of a myriad of humanitarian assistance and psychological interventions, recovery is often without structural absorption. Therefore, both individually and collectively, the fabric that binds society together and the traditional practices and grass roots social relations are shattered, dissociated, and disordered, making communities helpless and hopeless.Third, the nature of the violent conflicts in SSA is unique and unconventional. Violence is perpetrated in communities, sometimes by people known to each other, and survivors, perpetrators, and victims are often difficult to distinguish (19–22). For instance, in the WAYS study in northern Uganda, both formerly abducted youth (perpetrators—involved in killings and mutilations) and those who were not abducted (victims—suffered atrocities at the hands of perpetrators) equally suffered from adverse mental health problems (19). This has significant implications for interventions to mitigate mental health problems among war-affected populations in SSA.Fourth, various subpopulations were affected differently by the war in northern Uganda at individual (personal), family, and community levels. At the individual level, the war affected various subpopulations differently (e.g., abducted vs. non-abducted; born in or out of captivity; perpetrator, victims, or victim/perpetrator; and sexually abused girls vs. sexually abused child mothers, among others). However, the majority of studies simply lumped all war-affected people together. For example, in a previous study with war-affected girls with a history of sexual violence and with children as a consequence, those who were sexually abused and with children had higher odds of reporting depressive or anxiety symptoms, somatic complaints, stigma, and general dysfunction than those who did not report sexual violence and do not have children (23). At the community level, discrimination and stigma are widespread, thus adversely affecting coping with the traumatic reactions and undermining reintegration and mental health help-seeking (23).Lastly, trauma is recognized in many African cultures not only as a behavioral or emotional issue but also as a spiritual and community one. The relationships between parties to a conflict or between the living and the dead are highlighted by this more expansive understanding of trauma (7, 8). For instance, despite the loss of loved ones, the primary causes of post-war stress for survivors of the war in northern Uganda were the deterioration of community values, which is still mourned more than the aspect of the violent conflict (7, 8).Although some previous studies (e.g., Bolton et al. (7)) have shown that Western therapies are effective in reducing symptoms, their primary focus has been on symptom reduction. The focus on symptom reduction limits the effectiveness of Western therapies in the context of CTS, which keeps on generating more symptoms or exacerbating the existing ones.This paper describes examples from Liberia, Mozambique, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, the Sudan, and Uganda. Examples of traditional rituals and ceremonies from these settings are illustrative rather than representative. Different communities in SSA may have their own traditional therapies for the treatment of trauma according to their culture, trauma appraisal, and meaning making. However, the common thread in the majority of traditional rituals and ceremonies is that they are directed toward promoting holistic healing, strengthening resilience, and building individual, family, and community capacities that enable survivors to cope with persistent stressors while fostering relationships, enhancing recovery, and improving wellbeing.Whereas symptoms such as nightmares and intrusion are understood as basic characteristics of PTSD in the West, among the people of northern Uganda, these are mediated through a spirit medium, Cen, a spirit of the dead that comes back to haunt the living for killing them or because they have not been given a decent burial (24). Consequently, traditional rituals such as ‘Mato Oput’ ceremonies to exorcise spirit possession, ‘Stepping on the egg’ to stop and decontaminate evil spirits, and giving someone a decent burial have been practiced for a long time among the Acholi community in northern Uganda (24, 25). The Acholi ‘Mato Oput’ ceremony promotes healing by restoring social cohesion, bolstering community support networks, encouraging reintegration, and making use of easily accessible local traditional resources that help long-term recovery in addition to addressing war trauma (25).In Mozambique, the Timhamba rituals and Magamba ceremonies conducted by specialized healers are used to counter spirit possession and address severe trauma and conflicts rooted in Mozambique’s civil war (26). On the other hand, in Liberia, the Zoes (traditional healers) treat mental illnesses in the communities (27, 28). In Sierra Leone, traditional rituals and cleansing ceremonies have been shown to work independently or together with Western therapies (29).In addition, in South Sudan, the Dinka community uses the Cieng ceremony to offer a holistic approach to trauma treatment, addressing both the social and physical aspects of psychological trauma. Social healing involves rituals to address the origins of the illness, while physical healing uses herbal remedies to relieve somatic symptoms. full_text_sections.abstract: Considerable knowledge has been generated on the symptoms, course, therapy, and care of survivors of traumatic experiences since posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) was added to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, third edition (DSM-III) in 1980. Notwithstanding this improved understanding, there is still disagreement over the definition, characteristics, and expression of PTSD in various settings. The aim of this paper was to offer a perspective on the limitations of the current conceptualization of mental health problems associated with continuous traumatic stress (CTS), considerations of contextual and cultural differences, and their implications for interventions. Particularly, this perspective aimed to address the generalization of Western therapies in non-Western societies, as well as the limitations of traditional rituals and ceremonies, and their limitations in the treatment of mental illness in the context of unending violent conflicts in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). In many traditional societies in SSA, trauma is experienced and symptoms are appraised based on the culture of survivors, demonstrating the importance of context in the conceptualization of CTS and the design of interventions. Psychological therapies in the majority of Western societies are based on symptom reduction, which are limited in the context of CTS and traditional cultures. The perspective also discusses different ecosystems in the treatment of trauma using Western and traditional society approaches, as well as the unique nature of the violent conflicts in SSA, and suggests a way forward. Finally, we discuss whether Western evidence-based therapies that are locally and culturally grounded and traditional rituals and ceremonies are mutually exclusive, particularly in the context of CTS and mass trauma that uniquely affect individuals, families, communities, and different subpopulations.
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionWhile PTSD and CPTSD are invaluable concepts in understanding the experiences of individuals who endured traumatic events, they may be limited for societies experiencing unending protracted violent conflicts. Comprehending the functional deficits associated with experiencing traumatic events and understanding the daily challenges that affect survivors, both at the community and individual levels, numerous stakeholders (e.g., individuals, families, the community, and cultural leaders) may be required in the design of interventions. Of critical importance is the reconstruction of the social fabric and pillars that once held societies together and are responsible for the diagnosis, prognosis, and care of survivors. In light of the complexity in the conceptualization of CTS in many theaters of conflicts in SSA where protracted traumatic events are dominant, a more contextualized and nuanced understanding of traumatic reactions may provide better treatment outcomes.Interventions to aid war-affected communities in regaining security, normalcy, and control while promoting community involvement and mobilizing internal resources to fulfill their needs are essential (48). Where the diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of mental health problems include the entire community; thus, interventions must be guided by conceptual clarity, contextual considerations, and community involvement. In many ethnic groups in SSA, healing is a systemic process that occurs at the individual, family, and community levels. Enhancing resilience, empowering individuals, and developing family and community capacities to help survivors deal with ongoing stressors are key pillars to sustaining the wellbeing of war-affected populations.

papers.title_original: When the war never ends: conceptual limitations, contextual differences and implications for interventions in continuous traumatic stress in Sub-Saharan Africa

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to offer a perspective on the limitations of the current conceptualization of mental health problems associated with continuous traumatic stress (CTS) and the implications of contextual and cultural differences for interventions in Sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The WAYS study is a longitudinal cohort study of the risks, protective factors, and trajectory of mental health problems in war-affected youths in northern Uganda since 2010.
analysis.methods: The study involved systematic review and meta-analyses of existing literature on PTSD and CTS in conflict-affected populations, with a focus on cultural and contextual differences in trauma appraisal and treatment.
analysis.main_results: The pooled prevalence of likely PTSD is estimated to be 22%, 30% in people who have experienced conflict, and 8% in those who have not experienced conflict.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the conceptualization of PTSD and CTS is limited in societies experiencing unending protracted violent conflicts, and that a more contextualized and nuanced understanding is needed for effective interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that interventions must be guided by conceptual clarity, contextual considerations, and community involvement to effectively address mental health problems in conflict-affected populations in Sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The variation in PTSD prevalence estimates is mainly driven by measurement heterogeneity, population selection, and timing, which limits the generalizability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This paper explores the conceptual limitations of PTSD and CTS in the context of continuous traumatic stress in Sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing the need for culturally adapted interventions. It highlights the importance of considering contextual and cultural differences in trauma appraisal and treatment, as well as the challenges of diagnosing PTSD in populations experiencing prolonged conflict. The study draws on the WAYS longitudinal cohort study in northern Uganda and existing literature to argue for a more nuanced understanding of traumatic reactions. It also discusses the potential of traditional rituals and ceremonies in complementing Western therapies. The paper notes that while Western interventions have shown symptom reduction, their long-term sustainability remains unclear. The findings suggest that interventions should be guided by conceptual clarity, contextual considerations, and community involvement. However, the study acknowledges limitations in the generalizability of its results due to measurement heterogeneity and varying study contexts.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在提供一种视角,探讨当前与持续创伤压力(CTS)相关的心理健康问题概念化方面的局限性,以及情境和文化差异对撒哈拉以南非洲地区干预措施的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: WAYS研究是一项自2010年以来对乌干达北部受战争影响青少年心理健康问题的风险、保护因素和轨迹进行的纵向研究(队列研究)。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过系统综述和荟萃分析现有文献,探讨冲突影响人群中创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)和持续创伤压力(CTS)的相关研究,重点关注创伤评估中的文化与情境差异以及精神疾病(治疗)的处理。
elements_zh.main_results: 可能患有创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)的综合患病率估计为22%,经历过冲突的人群中为30%,未经历过冲突的人群中为8%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在经历持续长期暴力冲突的社会中,对创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)和持续创伤压力(CTS)的概念化存在局限,需要更情境化和细致的理解以实现有效的干预措施。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,干预措施必须以概念清晰性、情境考量和社区参与为指导,以有效应对撒哈拉以南非洲地区冲突影响人群的心理健康问题。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: PTSD患病率(患病率)估计值的差异主要由测量方法的异质性、人群选择和时间因素驱动,这限制了研究结果的普遍适用性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在提供一种视角,探讨当前与持续创伤压力(CTS)相关的心理健康问题概念化方面的局限性,以及情境和文化差异对撒哈拉以南非洲地区干预措施的影响。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: WAYS研究是一项自2010年以来对乌干达北部受战争影响青少年心理健康问题的风险、保护因素和轨迹进行的纵向研究(队列研究)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究通过系统综述和荟萃分析现有文献,探讨冲突影响人群中创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)和持续创伤压力(CTS)的相关研究,重点关注创伤评估中的文化与情境差异以及精神疾病(治疗)的处理。
analysis_zh.main_results: 可能患有创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)的综合患病率估计为22%,经历过冲突的人群中为30%,未经历过冲突的人群中为8%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在经历持续长期暴力冲突的社会中,对创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)和持续创伤压力(CTS)的概念化存在局限,需要更情境化和细致的理解以实现有效的干预措施。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,干预措施必须以概念清晰性、情境考量和社区参与为指导,以有效应对撒哈拉以南非洲地区冲突影响人群的心理健康问题。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: PTSD患病率(患病率)估计值的差异主要由测量方法的异质性、人群选择和时间因素驱动,这限制了研究结果的普遍适用性。

Angola Journalists visit COESP and bolster the response to Mpox in Angola 5 October 2026 | News Release | Reading time: 3 min Journalists visit COESP and bolster the response to Mpox in Angola More pictures More images Angola continues to bolster its response to the Mpox outbreak, which has so far resulted in 796 confirmed cases and two deaths since 2024, according to figures released by the health authorities. Against this backdrop, journalists from various media organizations visited the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COESP) in Luanda as part of an initiative by the Angolan Government to strengthen risk communication and the public’s access to reliable information about the disease. The visit enabled participants to learn about how the COESP operates and its role in coordinating public health emergencies. The center collates data from epidemiological surveillance, monitors the progression of outbreaks, and supports health authorities in their decision-making. According to the WHO Representative in Angola, Dr. Indrajit Hazarika, the effectiveness of the response to an emergency depends on the ability to turn information into action quickly. In this context, COESP plays a central role in gathering and analyzing data that guides the national response to the outbreak. “The sooner we identify an outbreak and the more quickly we mobilise the necessary resources, the greater our ability to interrupt transmission and save lives. The epidemiological surveillance data analyzed at COESP informs decisions on case investigation, vaccination, treatment, risk communication, and the mobilization of teams,” he said. As the country steps up its efforts to control the spread of Mpox, communication is becoming an essential component of the response. Clear and timely information helps the public to recognize the symptoms of the disease, understand how it is transmitted, and adopt preventive measures. In this process, journalists play an important role in translating technical information into accessible messages and in promoting verified content that helps to reduce rumors and misinformation. Addressing media professionals, the Secretary of State for Health, Dr. Carlos Pinto de Sousa, highlighted the importance of responsible coverage during the outbreak and called for the dissemination of accurate, evidence-based information. “It is essential that the media continue to play their part in disseminating accurate, clear and evidence-based information, helping to inform the public, promote preventive measures and reduce misinformation and public alarm,” he said. The WHO continues to support the Ministry of Health in strengthening epidemiological surveillance, risk communication, and mechanisms for coordinating the response to Mpox. Collaboration between health authorities, partners, and the media is essential to ensure that communities receive reliable information and can make informed decisions to protect their health. Mpox is a viral disease transmitted mainly through close contact with an infected person, including direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, or contaminated objects. Although most cases present with mild to moderate symptoms, the disease can cause serious complications in the most vulnerable people. Given that the virus is circulating in several African countries, early case detection, contact tracing, evidence-based communication, and community engagement remain crucial to limiting transmission and controlling the outbreak. analysis.time: The mpox outbreak in Uganda has been ongoing for 118 days since its start in 2024, with the latest situation update published on 19 November 2024. The publication date of the report is 11 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is reported in Uganda, specifically across 45 districts. The age group most affected is 19-39 years old, comprising 58% of confirmed cases.
analysis.event: A confirmed mpox outbreak has been reported in Uganda, with 582 confirmed cases and two deaths recorded. The event is reported by the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Africa.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak has resulted in 582 confirmed cases and two deaths. The affected population includes individuals across 45 districts, with the 19-39 years age group being the most impacted. The risk is not explicitly stated in the evidence, but the outbreak is ongoing and has caused significant public health concern.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The situation update indicates that the outbreak is being monitored and reported by the WHO Regional Office for Africa. There is no mention of specific response measures or investigation status beyond the reporting of cases and deaths.

analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Africa has reported a confirmed mpox outbreak in Uganda, which has been ongoing for 118 days since its start in 2024. As of 19 November 2024, 582 confirmed cases and two deaths have been recorded across 45 districts. The age group most affected is 19-39 years old, making up 58% of all confirmed cases. The outbreak has raised public health concerns, but the report does not specify the exact risk level. The situation update was published on 11 October 2026, indicating ongoing monitoring and reporting by WHO. No detailed response measures or investigation status are provided in the evidence.

news.content: Jump to Key Points Cases of clade Ib mpox have increased in the US over the past several months, and this increase is likely to continue, on the basis of the latest data from the CDC. In early September, the CDC reported more than 60 cases of clade I mpox across at least 20 states. As of the CDC’s October 5 update , this number had increased to 80. Most mpox cases in the US continue to occur in men who are gay or bisexual or men who have sex with men (MSM), and many cases involve individuals who have traveled from areas of mpox outbreaks in Central and Eastern Africa or parts of Western Europe where outbreaks have been reported. Consequently, the risk to the general public remains low, and the risk to MSM is low to moderate, according to the CDC. However, an increasing proportion of US cases have occurred among people with no recent international travel or known links to recent travelers, suggesting the virus is spreading domestically. The CDC noted on its website that these cases indicate “a likely transition toward sustained transmission in the United States,” with presumed domestic transmission reported in more than 10 jurisdictions. What’s Driving the Change? Two key elements are converging in mpox epidemiology, said Jason Zucker, MD, assistant professor of medicine in the Division of Infectious Diseases at Columbia University Irving Medical Center in New York City and the corresponding author of a 2024 review of mpox diagnosis and treatment published in JAMA . SUGGESTED FOR YOU First, the number of places from which individuals may acquire clade Ib is increasing. It has been spreading in Western Europe since approximately last fall; therefore, an exposure during travel to Spain or Netherlands matters as much as travel to Central Africa, he said. Second, the virus spreads quickly once it arises in a sexual network, as seen in the 2022 outbreak, said Zucker. Prior infection and vaccination make similar spikes unlikely even with the current increase in cases, he said. However, “we can still see spread between vulnerable individuals who come in close physical contact, and most people acquiring infection are still unvaccinated,” he added. Genomic data from the 2025 California cluster showed a single introduction leading to local spread, and the recent rise in cases is likely that pattern repeating in multiple places at once, said Zucker. “Mild or unrecognized illness may also play a role,” he noted. Clade Ib cases outside of Africa have mainly been mild, especially among those previously vaccinated, he said. “A person with a few lesions who is not asked about mpox may never get tested, and transmission continues undetected,” he explained. What Clinicians Should Know Although the overall risk in the general population remains low, the takeaway for clinicians is to get a lesion swab for mpox polymerase chain reaction testing for any new vesicular, pustular, or ulcerative rash in someone with a possible exposure; clinicians should know how their lab reports clade-specific results. “A result that is orthopoxvirus positive but clade II negative is clade I until proven otherwise,” Zucker said. Management of patients with mpox has not changed, and the standard remains supportive care and pain control, with CDC consultation for individuals who are immunocompromised to explore experimental antivirals. Prevention is the most important factor, Zucker said. For at-risk patients who are eligible, use every office visit to offer and complete the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine series, he advised. The right message for patients is that mpox is preventable and manageable, he added. “The clade Ib we are seeing has not presented the same historically; more than 300 cases have been diagnosed in high-income countries without a single death,” said Zucker. However, those most likely to become very sick represent the same group as those reported in 2022 — individuals with advanced HIV disease, especially those with a CD4 count < 200, and anyone who is immunocompromised — and for those patients, getting both vaccine doses before an exposure is critical, as well as early diagnosis and supportive care, he said. Research Gaps The STOMP trial , on which Zucker served as vice chair, showed that tecovirimat was not effective against clade II mpox. More research is needed to acquire prospective data on how clade Ib differs from clade IIb in transmissibility and severity, he said. Other research needs include vaccine effectiveness estimates, especially on the duration of two-dose protection. Tecovirimat did not work, so no drug is currently available to help the immunocompromised people who need treatment the most, he said. Zucker reported receiving research funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the CDC for mpox, serving as vice chair of the NIH-funded STOMP trial of tecovirimat for mpox, and receiving research funding at his institution from Gilead Sciences. news.source_body_en: The article discusses the increasing number of mpox clade Ib cases in the United States, as reported by the CDC. As of October 5, 2026, over 80 cases have been documented across at least 20 states, with a growing proportion of cases occurring among individuals without recent international travel or known exposure to travelers. This suggests a shift toward domestic transmission. The CDC emphasizes that the risk to the general public remains low, but the risk for men who are gay or bisexual or men who have sex with men (MSM) is low to moderate. Most cases outside of Africa have been mild, particularly among those previously vaccinated, but individuals with advanced HIV disease or immunocompromised status are still at higher risk. Clinicians are advised to conduct mpox polymerase chain reaction testing for any new rash in patients with possible exposure and to be aware of clade-specific results. The article also highlights the importance of prevention, including the JYNNEOS vaccine, and notes that no effective antiviral treatment is currently available for immunocompromised individuals. The findings are based on genomic data and epidemiological trends, with the CDC monitoring the situation closely.
news.content_zh: 本文讨论了美国报告的猴痘 Ib型病例数量不断增加的情况,据美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)报告。截至2026年10月5日,已有超过80例病例在至少20个州被记录,其中越来越多的病例出现在没有近期国际旅行或已知接触旅行者的人群中。这表明该病毒正在向国内传播转变。CDC强调,对一般公众的风险仍然较低,但对同性性行为男性(包括男同性恋、双性恋和男男性行为者,即MSM)的风险为低至中等。除非洲外,大多数病例较为轻微,尤其是之前接种过疫苗的人群,但艾滋病晚期或免疫功能低下的人群仍面临较高风险。临床医生被建议对可能有暴露的患者出现的新皮疹进行猴痘聚合酶链式反应(PCR)检测,并注意与特定亚型相关的检测结果。本文还强调了预防的重要性,包括JYNNEOS 疫苗疫苗,并指出目前尚无有效的抗病毒药物 治疗疫苗可用于免疫功能低下的人群。这些发现基于基因组数据和流行病学趋势,CDC正在密切监测这一情况。

analysis_zh.time: 截至CDC于2026年10月5日的更新,美国猴痘 I型病例数量已增加至80例。根据CDC最新的数据,病例数量可能还会继续增加。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 病例报告涉及美国至少20个州,其中大多数病例出现在同性性行为男性(包括男同性恋、双性恋和男男性行为者,即MSM)中,许多病例涉及来自中非和东非地区或西欧部分地区的旅行者。
analysis_zh.event: 过去几个月,CDC报告称美国猴痘 Ib型病例数量有所增加,特别是那些没有近期国际旅行或与近期旅行者有已知联系的人群中病例显著上升,表明病毒正在国内传播。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: CDC指出,对一般公众的风险仍然较低,而对MSM的风险为低至中等。除非洲外,Ib型病例主要为轻度,尤其是之前接种过疫苗的人群,但艾滋病晚期或免疫功能低下的人群仍面临较高风险。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC正在监测病毒的传播情况,并指出美国可能正在向持续的传播转变。临床医生被建议对可能有暴露的人出现的新水疱、脓疱或溃疡性皮疹进行猴痘聚合酶链式反应(PCR)检测,并注意与特定亚型相关的检测结果。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 9, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Children Bore a Hidden Share of Sierra Leone’s Clade IIb Mpox Outbreak by October 9, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Children Bore a Hidden Share of Sierra Leone's Clade IIb Mpox Outbreak Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram When mpox swept through Sierra Leone in 2024 and 2025, the global assumption that the clade IIb virus circulating there was primarily an adult problem was quietly overturned. A retrospective national study published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases has now documented 415 children younger than 15 years among 5,466 cases with recorded age, meaning children accounted for 7.6 percent of the outbreak’s known burden. The finding matters because the 2022 multicountry global outbreak, which was driven largely by sexual networks among adults, reported children and adolescents as only about 1.3 percent of cases. Sierra Leone’s experience shows that during a sustained African clade IIb epidemic, household transmission can pull young children into the epidemiological picture at rates several times higher than the world saw in 2022, and that surveillance systems built around adult-centered assumptions risk underestimating and under-serving this vulnerable group. The research team, led by investigators at Sierra Leone’s National Public Health Agency, assembled their cohort from the national District Health Information Software 2 database, the country’s integrated disease surveillance backbone, and then enriched it with patient charts and the original outbreak-investigation forms completed by district response teams. The analysis covered a database extract frozen on 1 July 2026, after the Ministry of Health declared the outbreak over in December 2025. Of the 415 paediatric cases, 411 were laboratory-confirmed, four were classified as probable, and none were clinician-diagnosed only. The age distribution was strikingly young: 188 children, or 45.3 percent, were aged 0 to 4 years, 121 were aged 5 to 9, and 106 were aged 10 to 14. The median paediatric age was just 5 years, and 230 of the 415 children, or 55.4 percent, were male. Discover more Buy Maps Track Outbreaks Shop African Art The temporal signal was equally telling. National surveillance summaries recorded only three sporadic paediatric cases of mpox-like illness between 2017 and 2024, a period when the disease was largely absent from the country. Notifications then rose sharply from April 2025 and peaked at 37 laboratory-confirmed paediatric cases in the epidemiological week ending 18 May 2025, before declining through June with a smaller resurgence in September and early October. Genomic analyses cited by the authors indicated that the clade IIb G.1 virus had been transmitting locally before public detection, which helps explain how an epidemic that appeared suddenly in adults had already seeded the household settings where young children are most exposed. The paediatric epidemic curve, in other words, was not an independent phenomenon but a mirror of the national outbreak, amplified through domestic contact networks. Discover more Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Find Family Lawyer Children Geographically, the burden concentrated in Western Area Urban, the densely populated district containing the capital Freetown, which recorded 195 of the 413 paediatric cases with known district, or 47.2 percent. Yet crude notified paediatric rates told a more nuanced story: Western Area Urban led at 80.2 notified cases per 100,000 estimated children, followed by the northern districts of Koinadugu at 60.5 and Falaba at 30.0. Together, Koinadugu, Falaba, and Karene accounted for 20.1 percent of paediatric cases but only 1.6 percent of cases among people aged 15 and older, a disproportionate paediatric share that the authors flag as a priority for field investigation. They caution, however, that these rates applied a single national age projection to every district, so if northern populations are younger than assumed, their paediatric denominators were underestimated and the rates overestimated. District-specific age denominators and testing data are needed before geographic differences can be read as true incidence. Clinically, the picture was dominated by fever and rash, each documented in 346 of 415 children, or 83.4 percent, with arm and leg lesions the most commonly reported sites. Secondary bacterial skin infection was documented in 36 children, or 8.7 percent, and one child developed acute respiratory distress syndrome. Care location was recorded for 285 children, of whom 216, or 75.8 percent, received hospital care for isolation, clinical management, or both, while 69 were managed at home. The authors emphasize that hospital admission in this outbreak did not necessarily signal severe disease, because admission frequently served isolation and infection-control purposes in crowded households where home isolation was impractical. Among 162 retrieved patient charts for hospitalized children, the median length of stay was 6 days, with an interquartile range of 4 to 9 days, and admission indication was available in 119 charts: isolation alone in 48, clinical management plus isolation in 62, and clinical management alone in 9. Discover more children child Hire Babysitters Outcomes were recorded for 261 children, and three died, a case fatality proportion of 1.1 percent with an exact 95 percent confidence interval of 0.2 to 3.3. The fatal cases shared a concerning pattern of delayed presentation, with onset-to-care intervals of 6, 15, and 27 days, and records described poor feeding or dehydration in two children, secondary bacterial skin infection in one, and moderate acute malnutrition in one. HIV status was unavailable for all three children who died, a gap that carries weight given a companion national analysis from the same team reporting fourfold or higher mpox mortality among people living with HIV during the outbreak. The authors argue that national records should distinguish admission purpose and standardize documentation of severity, treatment, complications, and recovery, because the emergency-era data could not fully separate the clinical course of mpox from the circumstances of delayed or inadequate care. The exposure analysis, drawn from 246 classifiable outbreak-investigation forms retrieved for 331 of the 415 children, pointed firmly toward the household. Household or caregiving contact, defined to include a household case, direct care, shared sleeping space, shared bedding or clothing, bathing, or feeding, was documented in 141 of 246 forms, or 57.3 percent. Another 48 children, or 19.5 percent, had several plausible exposures with no single predominant source, 39, or 15.9 percent, reported school, peer, or community contact, 12, or 4.9 percent, reported animal, wildlife, or bushmeat exposure, and 6, or 2.4 percent, reported health-care contact. Notably, eight of the twelve animal-related records came from Koinadugu or Falaba, hinting at rural exposure patterns that differ from the urban household transmission dominating Western Area Urban. With 188 children younger than 5 in this cohort alone, they argue that Sierra Leone’s future guidance should define eligibility for exposed younger children under applicable national authorization, with prospective safety and effectiveness monitoring. After deduplicating surveillance fields, 55 of the 415 children had documented genital or perianal lesions, and the DHIS2 field labelled vaginal lesions was marked for 43 of 185 girls, most often among those aged 10 to 14. news.title: Hong Kong records 21 mpox cases since August, high-risk groups urged to get jabs - South China Morning Post
news.rss_summary_html: Hong Kong records 21 mpox cases since August, high-risk groups urged to get jabs  South China Morning Post
news.excerpt_original: Hong Kong records 21 mpox cases since August, high-risk groups urged to get jabs South China Morning Post
news.priority_tier_reason: 可信机构来源或已成功抓获正文
news.content: Hong Kong has recorded 21 cases of mpox since August, accounting for 70 per cent of this year’s total, prompting health authorities to urge people who engage in high-risk sexual contact to take protective measures and get vaccinated to reduce their risk of infection. The latest case, involving a 29-year-old man, brought the total number recorded in Hong Kong this year to 30, comprising 23 local cases and seven imported ones, the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) said on Saturday. Twenty-one cases, or 70 per cent of the total, were recorded since August. Epidemiological investigations showed that all 21 patients reported engaging in high-risk sexual behaviour during the incubation period, including having sex with male strangers or multiple partners, and having sex without a condom, the centre said. View in App READ FULL ARTICLE Most of the patients had not been vaccinated against mpox, it added. Genetic analysis of the virus also found that some cases had identical genetic sequences, suggesting they might have shared a common source of infection, with multiple transmission chains existing among the population of men who have sex with men. “The CHP once again urges individuals who have engaged in high-risk sexual contact, particularly with strangers, to remain vigilant and take appropriate personal protective measures, including receiving the mpox vaccination and avoiding high-risk sexual contact, so as to lower the risk of infection,” it said. The centre also noted that more than half of the patients diagnosed in recent months with mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, had used dating apps to find casual sexual partners. “In some cases, patients were unable to contact their newly met sexual partners, which hinders effective contact tracing and the implementation of corresponding prevention and control measures,” it said. It urged people to keep their sexual partners’ contact details to make contact tracing easier. The latest case under investigation involved a 29-year-old man who developed a papule – a small, solid, raised bump – on his buttock on September 28. He later developed rashes on his limbs and buttock, as well as a fever and swollen lymph nodes. He attended an outreach vaccination service organised by the centre on October 8. Staff noticed his symptoms and arranged for him to receive isolation treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital in Kwai Chung. His clinical specimen tested positive for the mpox virus. The patient was in a stable condition, the centre said. He had high-risk sexual contact with a man in Hong Kong during the incubation period, it added. The centre said it was continuing its epidemiological investigation of the case and would report it to the World Health Organization. Hong Kong has recorded 114 mpox cases – 90 local and 24 imported – since 2022, all involving male patients. Mpox is a zoonosis – an infectious disease that can be transmitted from animals to humans – caused by the monkeypox virus. Infection can occur through contact with the virus from infected animals or people, or contaminated materials. People can become infected through bites or scratches from certain wild animals, such as some species of primates, rodents and squirrels, or through direct contact with their body fluids. Human-to-human transmission is mainly through close contact with infected individuals, such as skin-to-skin, mouth-to-mouth, mouth-to-skin and sexual contact. The likelihood of transmission through respiratory droplets is relatively low. The Department of Health provides mpox vaccination services for high-risk groups, including people who engage in high-risk sexual practices, such as having multiple sexual partners, sex workers or people who have had a sexually transmitted infection in the past 12 months

news.title_zh: 香港自8月起记录21例猴痘病例,高风险群体被敦促接种疫苗 - 南华早报
news.source_body_en: Hong Kong has recorded 21 mpox cases since August 2026, accounting for 70% of the year's total, prompting health authorities to urge high-risk sexual groups to take protective measures and get vaccinated. The latest case involved a 29-year-old man who developed symptoms on September 28 and was isolated at Princess Margaret Hospital. All 21 patients reported engaging in high-risk sexual behavior, including unprotected sex with multiple partners or strangers. Genetic analysis revealed some cases shared identical sequences, suggesting a common source and multiple transmission chains among men who have sex with men. The CHP emphasized the importance of keeping sexual partner contact details for effective contact tracing and prevention. Most patients had not been vaccinated, and the center is continuing its investigation and will report to the World Health Organization.
news.content_zh: 自2026年8月以来,香港已记录21例猴痘病例,占全年总数的70%,促使卫生部门敦促高风险性行为群体采取防护措施并进行疫苗接种。最新病例是一名29岁男子,于9月28日出现症状,并在玛格丽特公主医院被隔离。所有21名患者均报告有高风险性行为,包括与多个性伴侣或陌生人发生无保护性行为。基因分析显示部分病例具有相同的序列,表明存在共同来源,并且在男男性行为者中存在多条传播传播链。警方强调保持性伴侣联系方式对于有效的接触者追踪和预防至关重要。大多数患者未接种疫苗,中心仍在继续调查并将向世界卫生组织报告。

Since the beginning of 2026, the city has recorded 30 cases of the disease, of which 23 are local and 7 are imported. Since 2022, the total number of infected has reached 114, all infections have been reported in men, most of whom have not been vaccinated. Experts from the Centre for Health Protection attribute the increase in cases to "high-risk sexual contacts." In response, the agency has intensified monitoring of the epidemiological situation and expanded the vaccination program. In the past two weeks, about 360 people from at-risk groups have been successfully vaccinated against monkeypox. The latest registered case concerns a 29-year-old man who was found to have skin rashes, a high fever, and swollen lymph nodes. The laboratory-confirmed condition of the patient is stable. The World Health Organization will be informed about this case. news.source_body_en: Hong Kong has experienced a sharp rise in monkeypox cases, with 21 new infections reported since August 2026, accounting for 70% of the total cases for the year. news.content_zh: 香港经历了猴痘病例的急剧上升,自2026年8月以来报告了21例新感染,占全年总病例数的70%。截至2026年10月11日,该市已记录30例病例,其中23例为本地病例,7例为输入病例。自2022年以来,香港的总感染人数已达114人,均为未接种疫苗的男性。专家将病例增加归因于“高风险性接触”。对此,香港卫生防护中心加强了监测,并扩大了疫苗接种计划。过去两周内,约有360名高风险群体成员接种了猴痘疫苗,最新病例涉及一名29岁男性,其症状包括皮疹、高烧和淋巴结肿大,实验室确诊状况稳定。世界卫生组织将被通知此病例。

news.content: 9°C clear sky TFL Updates Search for: Search Search LDN Write For Us Login London News Lifestyle Entrepreneurship Fitness & Health Finance Tech Food & Drink Automotive Travel Global UK mpox update records September cases as clade Ib becomes more common By LDN Editor 10 October 2026 4 minute read Listen to this article The UK Health Security Agency’s 8 October mpox surveillance update records cases through 30 September 2026, continuing a revised clade presentation introduced in August. Clade Ib has become more common than clade IIb in the country. The national figures place London at the centre of England’s regional picture but do not include a current London case total. From August, the UK Health Security Agency’s reporting presentation separates confirmed clade Ib, confirmed clade IIb, recombinant clades and cases whose clade is not yet known. Earlier reports grouped cases with an unconfirmed clade alongside clade IIb. The change reflects an epidemiological shift: UK clade Ib case numbers increased during 2026 and exceeded clade IIb from July. The new format is important when comparing figures across reports. A category described as “not yet known” should not be read as a new strain, while a change in how cases are grouped can affect apparent comparisons over time. The revised presentation gives readers a clearer separation of confirmed clades and cases still awaiting classification. National figures through September The cumulative UK total from 6 May 2022 to 30 September 2026 is 5,023 cases. That total includes 3,732 cases recorded in 2022 and 1,291 across 2023 to September 2026. In the latter period, 226 cases were classified as clade Ib, 972 as clade IIb and 93 as clade not yet known. These are different time spans and should not be conflated. England accounted for 1,168 of the 1,291 cases recorded across the UK from 2023 to September 2026. Within England, 585 were presumed to have been acquired in the UK, 375 were presumed imported and 208 were awaiting classification. The remaining cases in that period were recorded in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. For September alone, England’s monthly dashboard lists 46 clade Ib cases, three clade IIb cases and 19 whose clade was not yet known. Those figures are for England, not London, and refer to the month commencing 1 September. They should not be presented as a London count or as a measure of prevalence at the time of publication. London’s place in the picture Across the period shown, most English cases were among people resident in London, although an increase was also seen in the north of England in early 2026. The overview does not provide a September London total, so the regional pattern cannot be converted into a precise local count. London also remains prominent in the vaccination data. By 31 March 2026, 63,624 first doses and 42,902 second doses had been administered to men who have sex with men in London. These are dose counts, not numbers of distinct people or completed courses. Most doses across England were administered in London, and the figures combine information from two surveillance systems covering different periods. The vaccination programme has changed over time. Reactive pre-exposure vaccination began in the UK in June 2022 for groups at higher risk of exposure. The national reactive offer ended in summer 2023, but continued in London and Greater Manchester in response to local transmission and case clusters. A routine national programme for men at higher risk attending specialist sexual health services began in England in August 2025. Reading the figures carefully The data are a surveillance snapshot, not a real-time count. The case tables were based on data extracted on 5 October, and later reports may include corrections arising from delayed reporting, updated patient information or removal of quality-assurance samples. Monthly case figures are assigned by specimen date. There is also a distinction between confirmed and highly probable cases. Clade IIb totals include both confirmed cases and highly probable cases identified through orthopox testing, so the total may be slightly higher than a count limited to confirmed mpox. The surveillance assessment treats the likely effect as minimal, while retaining that classification caveat. The figures describe reported cases and vaccine doses; they do not, on their own, establish the risk to any individual or explain why cases changed. The revised clade presentation and the September figures offer a more current national view, while the London data show the city’s continuing significance in both regional case patterns and vaccination activity. analysis.time: The UK Health Security Agency’s mpox surveillance update was published on 8 October 2026, and the data covers cases through 30 September 2026. The September figures refer to the month commencing 1 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The data focuses on the UK, with London being central to England’s regional picture. The affected population includes men who have sex with men, particularly in London, and cases are distributed across England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales.
analysis.event: The UK Health Security Agency updated its mpox surveillance data, noting that clade Ib has become more common than clade IIb in the country. The report highlights an epidemiological shift with clade Ib case numbers increasing and surpassing clade IIb from July 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: From 6 May 2022 to 30 September 2026, the UK recorded 5,023 mpox cases, including 226 classified as clade Ib and 972 as clade IIb in the period from 2023 to September 2026. For September 2026 alone, England reported 46 clade Ib cases, three clade IIb cases, and 19 cases with an unknown clade. The surveillance data does not establish individual risk levels but indicates a shift in clade prevalence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The UK Health Security Agency revised its reporting format in August 2026 to separate confirmed clade Ib, confirmed clade IIb, recombinant clades, and cases with unknown clades. The data is a surveillance snapshot, not real-time, and may include corrections from delayed reporting or updated patient information. The report emphasizes that the figures should not be interpreted as a precise local count for London.

From 6 May 2022 to 30 September 2026, the UK recorded 5,023 mpox cases, with clade Ib becoming more common than clade IIb. The report notes that clade Ib case numbers exceeded clade IIb from July 2026. While the national figures show London as central to the regional pattern, no specific September London case count is provided. The data includes 226 clade Ib cases and 972 clade IIb cases from 2023 to September 2026, with 46 clade Ib cases reported in England for September 2026. The surveillance data is a snapshot and may include corrections. The report also mentions London’s prominence in vaccination efforts, with 63,624 first doses and 42,902 second doses administered to men who have sex with men by 31 March 2026. The figures do not establish individual risk levels but reflect an epidemiological trend. The revised reporting format aims to clarify clade classifications and improve data comparability across reports.

Local 29-year-old man diagnosed with Mpox after attending outreach vaccination service in Mong Kok By Dickson Tam - 3:12PM Sat October 10, 2026 254 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Pinterest Telegram 10th October 2026 – (Hong Kong) The Centre for Health Protection of the Department of Health has confirmed a new Mpox case involving a 29-year-old man in Hong Kong. The patient developed a papule on his buttock on 28th September, with subsequent rashes, fever, and swollen lymph nodes. On 8th October, while attending an outreach vaccination service jointly held by the Centre for Health Protection and the Hong Kong Christian Service, his symptoms were noticed by medical staff who arranged for immediate isolation and treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital. Subsequent laboratory tests confirmed a positive result for Monkeypox virus, and the patient is currently in a stable condition. close Advertisements dimsumdailyhk [custom chain] curation-20261008-09:06 arrow_forward_ios Read More CANCEL NEXT VIDEO play_arrow volume_mute AD PausePlay % buffered00:00 00:01 01:32 UnmuteMute Play Epidemiological investigation revealed that the man had engaged in high-risk sexual activities with a male partner in Hong Kong during the incubation period. The Centre for Health Protection is continuing its investigation and will notify the World Health Organization of the case. This diagnosis forms part of a larger recent increase in the number of Mpox cases in the city. Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 114 cases, all male, with 30 reported in 2026 alone. Of these, 23 are local cases and seven have been imported, and 21 out of the recent cases have occurred since August, representing 70 per cent of the annual total. Investigations indicate these recent cases commonly involve high-risk sexual practices, with many patients having found casual male partners using dating applications, and most had not previously received the Mpox vaccine. The Centre for Health Protection has increased its prevention and response measures amid this surge. In addition to expanding existing vaccination venue services and outreach, new vaccination sites have been established, including an additional centre at the CHP Building and collaboration with three non-governmental organisations, notably the Hong Kong AIDS Foundation and Hong Kong Christian Service. Over the past two weeks, approximately 360 high-risk individuals have received the Mpox vaccine. The next outreach session with the Hong Kong AIDS Foundation is scheduled for 14th October at the Mong Kok Service Centre, and an additional session will be held at the Yau Ma Tei Integrated Treatment Centre on 24th October. The authorities have also stepped up public education, providing daily telephone hotlines for advice and vaccination arrangements and working with online dating platforms to promote safe practices and vaccination information within the community. With more than half of recent patients admitting to being unable to contact their new sexual partners, the Centre for Health Protection has urged the public to retain contact information for partners to facilitate effective contact tracing. Members of the public, especially those at high risk, are encouraged to limit the number of sexual partners, use condoms and receive vaccination to reduce the risk of infection and help contain the current outbreak. news.title_zh: 29岁男子确诊猴痘,曾参加 Mong Kok 的 疫苗接种 服务 - Dimsum Daily
news.source_body_en: A 29-year-old man in Hong Kong has been diagnosed with Mpox after attending an outreach vaccination service in Mong Kok. The Centre for Health Protection confirmed the case, and the patient was isolated and treated at Princess Margaret Hospital. The patient developed a papule on his buttock on 28th September, with subsequent rashes, fever, and swollen lymph nodes. His symptoms were noticed on 8th October during the vaccination service. The diagnosis is part of a larger recent increase in Mpox cases in the city, with 30 cases reported in 2026 alone. Of these, 23 are local cases, and 7 have been imported. The outbreak is linked to high-risk sexual activities, with many patients having found casual male partners through dating apps and not previously vaccinated. The Centre for Health Protection has increased prevention and response measures, including expanding vaccination services and establishing new sites. They have also urged the public to retain contact information for sexual partners to aid contact tracing. The authorities are working with online dating platforms to promote safe practices and vaccination information within the community.

news.content: Azernews.Az Monday, October 12, 2026 Login Latest NATION WORLD BUSINESS OIL & GAS ARMENIAN-AZERBAIJANI RELATIONS EDITORIAL ANALYSIS LIFESTYLE EVENTS HEALTHCARE CULTURE SPORTS OUR WRITERS Health authorities monitor rising mpox cases in Hong Kong 11 October 2026 10:29 (UTC+04:00) Ulviyya Poladova Read more New cases of mpox have been reported in Hong Kong, according to local health authorities. Since August, 21 new infections have been recorded, accounting for 70 percent of all cases reported in 2026. "Since 2022, a total of 114 mpox cases have been identified in Hong Kong. All patients have been male. Thirty cases have been recorded so far this year," the statement said. In response to the significant rise in infections, targeted prevention and control measures are being implemented through a multi-pronged approach. The number of vaccinations administered has also been increasing. Medical experts have urged the public to remain vigilant and take precautions to help prevent further spread of the disease. Mpox is a rare viral disease that occurs mainly in remote areas of Central and West Africa, particularly those near tropical rainforests. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the virus can spread to humans from wild animals, including rodents and primates, while human-to-human transmission has historically been limited. The case fatality rate during mpox outbreaks has generally ranged from 1% to 10%, with most deaths occurring among younger age groups. Search Spanish News / Health / Mpox death in Euskadi leaves cause unresolved 5 mins read Published October 9, 2026, 9:03 PM Mpox death in Euskadi leaves cause unresolved Post by Richard Reid Mpox death in Euskadi leaves cause unresolved © russpain.com Share Facebook X WhatsApp Copy link Reddit A 61-year-old man died at Hospital de Donostia after contracting mpox. Cancer, severe immune suppression and a suspected hospital exposure have complicated the search for the direct cause. On 6 October, a 61-year-old man died at Hospital de Donostia after more than a month in hospital. Whether mpox directly caused his death remains unresolved. He had been receiving treatment for throat cancer and was immunosuppressed. The Basque Department of Health said a direct causal link cannot be confirmed, although the likelihood is considered high. Doctors stressed that he died “with mpox”, not necessarily “from mpox”. More than 30 people linked to the hospital room have been vaccinated and placed under follow-up. The group includes healthcare workers and people from the patients’ circles who were considered at risk. The deceased man was reportedly vaccinated as well. Osakidetza tracked about 50 potential contacts in connection with the hospital exposure, a wider group than the roughly 30 people who received vaccination. Osakidetza The suspected transmission route remains uncertain. The man entered the hospital on 1 September because of a throat tumour. After surgery, he suffered bleeding that required two further operations. His family said his recovery initially appeared positive. He had started rehabilitation in the hospital gym and was expected to begin speech therapy in October. His serious underlying illness and severely weakened condition were important factors in assessing the possible consequences of the infection. The possible exposure occurred after he shared a room for less than a week with another patient identified as the index case. That patient had also been admitted because of a throat complication. Hospital sources said he initially had no characteristic skin lesions associated with monkeypox, although he did have an infectious condition. Miguel Ángel Goenaga, head of infectious diseases at Hospital de Donostia, said mpox generally has low mortality, but its consequences can be substantially more serious in people with major underlying illnesses and severely reduced immunity. Miguel Ángel GoenagaHead of infectious diseases at Hospital de Donostia According to the family, masks began appearing among staff after several days of ordinary contact between the two patients. Staff later told the family that the roommate had tested positive during a routine examination and had been discharged to isolate at home. The hospital then identified people who might have been exposed and activated the required measures. Osakidetza followed about 50 potential contacts, including medical workers and people from the patients’ circles. Authorities consider new linked cases very unlikely after the preventive measures. After the patients were separated, the 61-year-old developed further bleeding or an infection linked to the throat operation. Two or three days after severe headaches began, spots appeared on his forehead. Lesions were also observed on his palms. An infectious diseases doctor and an internist assessed him before he was isolated in the infectious diseases unit. Doctors later returned him to the other ward because treatment of the throat problem was considered more urgent. His condition then worsened, and he was transferred to intensive care. Family members said he did not recover despite antibiotics. He also received antiviral medication and morphine. Miguel Ángel Goenaga, head of infectious diseases at Hospital de Donostia, did not identify a precise transmission mechanism when speaking to the media. He said infection generally requires close contact and that hospital transmission is uncommon. Possible explanations included contact between the patients at night. The exchange of an object was another possibility. Other routes were considered less important in this setting. One involved prolonged face-to-face contact through respiratory secretions. Another involved direct contact with contaminated objects. Transmission from a pregnant mother to a fetus through the placenta was also considered less important. The case arrives as infections rise again in Euskadi. The region recorded 245 cases in 2022, followed by one diagnosis in 2023 and 12 in 2024. Six people were diagnosed in 2025. The first nine months of 2026 produced 35 cases, including eight in Gipuzkoa. Figures reported by Euskadi’s health authorities show a marked increase in detection during 2026, although the available reports do not explain its cause. Two other people have died from monkeypox in Spain this year. Monkeypox is caused by the monkeypox virus and usually spreads through close physical contact rather than brief exposure in a shared space. Common symptoms include fever and headache. Muscle pain and back pain are also reported. Other symptoms include swollen lymph nodes, chills and exhaustion. A rash can spread from the face to other parts of the body. The illness generally lasts two to four weeks, and most patients recover. The family account reconstructs a complicated hospital course but does not establish that monkeypox was the direct cause of death. The patient had a serious cancer diagnosis and underwent repeated surgery before the infection was identified. The Basque Department of Health and the official Osakidetza account have therefore kept the cause of death under assessment, while independent reports confirm the suspected hospital infection without establishing the exact transmission mechanism. The case is distinct from the earlier Madrid investigation covered in a separate report. Euskadi has recorded its first death involving monkeypox, while the infection’s exact role remains unproven. Sources said the latest victim is a 50-year-old man from Qazi Ahmed, Nawabshah. He is currently under treatment at the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital & Research Centre. “He is referred to us by the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre. His condition is not good due to chronic kidney disease,” a senior doctor at the hospital said, adding that he had been on dialysis. Data released by Provincial Disease Surveillance and Response Unit showed that 11 deaths have been reported so far this year. It showed Karachi is the most mpox-affected city with 26 cases followed by 22 in Khairpur and nine in Sukkur. The monthly trend showed that April saw the largest number of cases (31) this year followed by September (20) and August (17). Seventy cases involved male patients and the most affected age-group was 30-39 years. “The health department is monitoring the situation and urges people to adopt precautionary measures. They should report immediately to a hospital in case symptoms appear,” said a statement.
